hypothesis: If the claim holds, then among obligate cave animals sampled from both America and Europe, each cave species' nearest relatives lie in the surface or cave fauna of its own continent more often than on the other continent, and the American and European cave faunas do not cluster with each other.
pass_criterion: In a dataset with phylogenetic placement for obligate cave species from both continents, at least 80% of cave species have their nearest sampled relative on the same continent. The proportion must also be significantly above the null expected from random continent assignment (permutation test, p < 0.05). Fewer than 10% of cave lineages may fall in a clade that is specially American-European.
fail_criterion: Fewer than 60% of cave species have their nearest relative on their own continent, or the same-continent proportion is not significantly above the permutation null (p >= 0.05). Cave taxa from the two continents must also not form transatlantic cave-specific clades more often than expected by chance.
interpretation: Darwin's 'blind cave animals' are read as obligate subterranean (troglobiont or stygobiont) species. 'Affinities to the other inhabitants of that continent' is read as a nearest relative, meaning a sister taxon or congener in a molecular phylogeny, located in the same continent's biota. The modern reinterpretation is a phylogenetic test of biogeographic affinity, using a sampled continent label per tip. The test needs both continents and sampled surface relatives. I found no public dataset that I could fetch and that meets this. The Dryad trechine beetle dataset (10.5061/dryad.sj3tx967w) was already judged American-only. Naming it, or any regional dataset, would test a weakened claim.
no_dataset_reason: Two further searches found only regional datasets. Examples are North American trechine beetles, Ozark grotto salamanders, North American cavefishes, and European spiders. None holds obligate cave species from both America and Europe together with sampled surface relatives or phylogenetic placement. A global stygofauna occurrence database appears in a conference abstract, but it has no phylogenetic placement and I did not fetch it. The trechine dataset page was fetched earlier by another attempt, not by me in this session. I name no dataset rather than test a weakened version of the claim.
